newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldiers keep tunnel open.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldiers keep tunnel open.

text.p: Israeli soldiers and paramilitary police lined the streets of Jerusalem's Old City on Sunday to ensure a controversial tunnel that triggered fierce Palestinian-Israeli bloodletting remained open.

Israeli troops in flak jackets securing the Old City's Moslem Quarter far outnumbered the tourists who emerged from a new entrance to the archaeological tunnel that Israel opened last week, sparking clashes which claimed close to 70 lives.

Most of those who passed through the 488-metre (534 yard)-long tunnel that reveals the foundations of the Temple Mount, once home to ancient Jewish temples and now site of Islam's al-Aqsa mosque, were religious Jews.

"Jerusalem belongs to the Jewish people and don't let anyone say any different," Tzvi Zucker told Reuters after stepping out of the tunnel onto the Via Dolorosa, the traditional path uopn which Jesus walked on the way to his crucifixion.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu decided to open the new entrance last week, drawing international condemnation and angering Palestinians who called it an assault on Islam's third holiest shrine. The move unleashed violent demonstrations and gunfights that have killed 55 Palestinians and 14 Israelis.
Some passing tourists were wary of the tunnel.
"I hear the Israeli police opened it...and it goes under the mosque. The Arabs don't like it," said Jose, a Spanish tourist.
Asked if he wanted to go inside, Jose said quickly: "No."
Other tourists dismissed the storm around the site.
"I think it's good they open the tunnel anyway," said Ingrid from Germany. "I think it's a reason Arafat used to want to have an intifada," she said, referring to the 1987-93 Palestinian uprising.

Netanyahu has accused Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat of "cynically" exploiting the tunnel issue and instigating the violence. Palestinians called the tunnel's opening an Israeli attempt to "Judaise" Arab East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.

Palestinians have appealed to the world to demand Israel shut the tunnel: "Keeping the tunnel open means pushing the whole region towards irresponsible violence," the PLO said in a statement issued on Saturday.
The previous centre-left Israeli government had avoided opening the tunnel because of Arab objections.
Netanyahu, who unseated the Labour-led government in May elections with a platform that opposed trading occupied Arab land for peace, refuses to close it.
"The tunnel has been around for 2,000 years...It will stay open. It will always be open," he told cheering Christian supporters Saturday night.
Earlier on Sunday, Palestinian youths hurled stones when the tunnel's new second entrance was opened after the Jewish sabbath. The protests were quickly quelled by police.
